brief: Goldman's daily covers three topics. Payroll preview: the bank estimates August nonfarm payrolls rose 40k against consensus of +55k, because big data job indicators slowed sequentially and August initial prints have carried a decade-long negative bias, partly offset by low layoffs and scope for rebounds in leisure and hospitality and local education. It forecasts unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, in line with consensus, on stabilizing continuing claims, and average hourly earnings up 0.4% month over month, above consensus, on calendar effects. Participation: most of the rise in people outside the labor force since January is college graduates over 55 retiring rather than discouraged workers, so the decline is less cyclically concerning. Composition shifts account for 0.2pp, 16-24 seasonality 0.1-0.2pp and 25-34 small sample bias 0.1pp of the 0.7pp decline since January. The note separately states these factors explain roughly 0.8 of a 1pp decline since December 2025. Europe: the 2026 STOXX EPS growth forecast was raised to 15%, normalizing to mid-single digits in 2027, risks skewed up. At 14.6x P/E and a 5.3% free cash flow yield against 3.6% for the S&P 500, Goldman stays constructive but selective, favoring Technology, Banks, Defense, Telecoms and Renewables, cautious on France, preferring Germany.
